record_type_quote: In light of a paucity of experimental research on the effects of culturally diverse children’s literature, there is a need to replicate and extend our prior work (Hardy et al., 2020). In the current study, we improved upon our previous methodology by creating sets of books that were identical, except for the skin color and hair texture of the protagonist, permitting us to control for the effects of extraneous variables related to stimuli within different books.

targets.authors: Hardy, J. K., Pennington, R., Griffin, R., & Jacobi-Vessels, J.
targets.title: Comparing the effects of protagonist race on preschoolers’ engagement in book reading.
targets.evidence_quote: In light of a paucity of experimental research on the effects of culturally diverse children’s literature, there is a need to replicate and extend our prior work (Hardy et al., 2020). In the current study, we improved upon our previous methodology by creating sets of books that were identical, except for the skin color and hair texture of the protagonist, permitting us to control for the effects of extraneous variables related to stimuli within different books.
targets.outcome_quote: Children’s engagement did not consistently vary based on protagonist race. However, of the four children with sufficient data to analyze book preference, all demonstrated a marked preference for books with a same-race protagonist.
targets.outcome_reasoning: Implicit comparison passes both tests: introduction explicitly states Hardy et al. (2020) found negligible engagement effects and selections biased toward same-skin-color protagonists. Current study likewise finds no consistent engagement differences and same-race preferences where sufficient choice data exist. No stated contrast to the original or overriding adverse verdict. Insufficient choice data for four children are a limitation, not a whole-study author verdict of uninformative.

reasoning: Full 25-page publisher article, including references, matches title, four authors and DOI. Systematic replication of the authors’ published 2020 paper using eight new preschoolers. Other cited studies motivate the work or supply methods; they are not additional tested originals.
